title: Grandparenting with arthritis and frailty (UK)
meta_description: Enjoying time with grandchildren when you have arthritis and frailty: seated activities, lifting safely, pacing visits and telling family what helps.
excerpt: Enjoying time with grandchildren when you have arthritis and frailty: seated activities, lifting safely, pacing visits and telling family what helps.
direct_answer: Arthritis and frailty can make lifting, chasing and long visits tiring. Seated activities, letting others lift, pacing and telling family what helps can keep time with grandchildren enjoyable.
author: Louis Maxwell
reviewer_credentials: First Contact Practitioner, HCPC PH128483, CSP member
keywords: grandparenting, grandchildren, arthritis, frailty, pacing, family, UK
content:
Time with grandchildren matters.

This guide covers practical ideas. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

Seated activities

  • Reading.
  • Games.
  • Crafts.

Lifting

Let others lift babies and toddlers; sit to cuddle.

Pacing visits

  • Shorter visits.
  • Rest afterwards.

Talking to family

Explain what helps.

When to get help

  • Call 999 for chest pain, trouble breathing, signs of a stroke, or a fall with a possible serious injury.
  • Get urgent advice the same day (NHS 111 or your GP) for sudden confusion, a sudden drop in mobility, or a hot, swollen joint with fever.
  • See your GP for a steady decline over weeks, unplanned weight loss or repeated falls.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Can I babysit?

Discuss what is safe.

What about baby equipment?

Choose items at waist height.

Sources and further reading

  • NHS: Tiredness and fatigue
  • NHS: 5 steps to mental wellbeing

Living With Arthritis is an independent charity and is not part of Arthritis UK (formerly Versus Arthritis). Everyone's situation is different, so follow the advice of your own GP and care team. If you feel very unwell, call 999 or go to A&E. For urgent advice, contact NHS 111 (NHS 24 on 111 in Scotland; in Northern Ireland, your GP or GP out-of-hours service).
